copy: The city finished bus lanes or busways on at least 15 other streets from 2023 through September 2026. The MTA’s monthly segment speeds can measure 11 of them. For each, the table compares buses on the treated street in the months after it opened with the same months before construction, then subtracts the change for the same routes on streets that got nothing new. The result is the net change. By that measure, eight of the 11 got faster, most by between 0.09 and 0.26 mph. Hillside Avenue in Queens gained the most, 0.62 mph, but it opened during the Queens bus network redesign. Madison Avenue gained 0.41 mph in its first three months. Gun Hill Road and Livingston Street changed little, and buses on Pelham Parkway got slower.
note: MTA Bus Route Segment Speeds, weekdays 7 a.m. to 7 p.m., weighted by trips. A route segment counts if at least half its length runs on the project. Each month after opening, up to 12 and through October 2026, is paired with the same month a year earlier, or two years earlier if that month fell during construction. These are whole-month MTA figures, a different source from the Flatbush GPS readings above. Four projects can’t be measured this way because the MTA’s segments through them are too long: Flatbush Avenue from Livingston to State streets (2025), Lexington Avenue from 52nd to 60th streets, Broadway in Queens and the Tremont Avenue busway (all 2026). City claims are from mayoral press releases in February and June 2026. A before-and-after comparison also picks up anything else that changed on the same street, such as signal timing or enforcement. Full results, with monthly series and every caveat.

projects.name: Northern Boulevard, Broadway to 114th Street
flags: Construction start unknown, so only January to July of each year are compared. Afternoon rush fell 3.7%.

projects.name: Gun Hill Road, Bainbridge Avenue to Bartow Avenue
flags: Construction began May 2023, leaving only January to April to compare.

projects.name: University Avenue, north section
flags: Bx3 only, with a small comparison set.

projects.name: Third Avenue, 59th to 96th streets
flags: Measured from 67th Street north only. Afternoon rush rose 4.9%.

projects.name: Pelham Parkway, Boston Road to Stillwell Avenue
flags: One 1.2-mile Bx12 local segment, westbound. Slower in all eight months compared.

projects.name: Livingston Street, Boerum Place to Flatbush Avenue
flags: B45 and B67 only; the B41’s MTA segments here run mostly off Livingston.

projects.name: 96th Street, crosstown
flags: Small comparison set; faster in eight of 12 months compared.

projects.name: Second Avenue, 59th Street to Houston Street
flags: Congestion pricing began Jan. 5, 2025, a month after the lanes opened, and this stretch is inside the zone.

projects.name: Third Avenue, 96th to 128th streets
flags: Faster in nine of 12 months compared.

projects.name: Hillside Avenue, 139th Street to Springfield Boulevard
flags: Opened during the Queens bus network redesign, which changed stops on these routes. Afternoon rush rose 17.9%.

projects.name: Madison Avenue, 23rd to 42nd streets
flags: Three months of data so far. Most of these buses are express routes.
